answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks by binding each identity to unique coordinates via multi-anchor radio ranging. Verifiers match nanosecond arrival times and multipath echoes to a terrain atlas, including diffraction off a basalt knoll, while enforcing minimum spacing between nodes. Creating fake identities thus requires deploying radio transceivers at separate sites per agent. However, seasonal foliage or moving vehicles distort multipath profiles and can misclassify valid nodes.
